chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman and Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who performs Hajj on behalf of another, and he commits something during his Hajj which necessitates that he performs Hajj again in the following year, or an expiation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It (the Hajj) is complete for the first one, and upon this one is what he committed.'
ai.seo_question: Who bears the penalty if someone performs Hajj on behalf of another and makes a mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distribution of liability in 'Hajj al-Badal' (substitute Hajj), establishing that the primary religious obligation is discharged for the principal, while any penalties incurred by the performer due to their own actions remain their personal responsibility. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of the act transfers to the beneficiary, but the accountability for defects or expiations rests with the agent, reflecting the distinct roles of obligation and execution in ritual law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Usman and Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who performs Hajj on behalf of another. So he commits something during his Hajj which necessitates him the Hajj in the future to be performed again, or an expiation. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It (Hajj) is complete for the first one, and upon this one is what he committed’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman and Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs al-Hajj for another person and he commits during performing al-Hajj something which obliges him to perform al-Hajj again in future or owes expiation. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is complete for the first one but he owes for whatever he has committed.’”
